findings.description: When ANSI is stripped, the code also calls `.strip()` on the whole prompt text. That removes the prompt's meaningful leading and trailing whitespace, including the usual trailing space (e.g. `"Name: "` becomes `"Name:"`).
findings.rationale: Trigger: a prompt such as `"Name: "` or `"Continue? [y/N]: "` shown on a non-tty stream or when color is disabled. `strip_ansi(text).strip()` drops the trailing space, so the user's input is typed directly against the colon. Leading indentation is lost too. Output differs depending on whether ANSI stripping is active, and `strip_ansi` alone would have been enough.
